71-00-03
F . Method 1 - Protective Coating Application
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU READ THE MANUFACTURER'S SAFETY DATA
SHEET (MSDS) FOR THE MATERIALS YOU WILL USE, AND WEAR THE
PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND EQUIPMENT IF IT IS SPECIFIED. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-002-F00
(1) If it is necessary, remove existing pitting, corrosion and surface oxidation from the inlet cowl
lipskin.
(a) Use the applicable Structural Repair Manual (SRM) procedure.
(b) Make sure that the minimum thickness requirements per the SRM are met.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-003-F00
(2) Prepare the lipskin for the application of X20-18 compound, G51625.
(a) Clean the lipskin with XS3 Aircraft Wash and XG5 Hard Surface Cleaner furnished from
the X20-18 compound, G51625, vendor prior to application.
NOTE: X20-18 compound, G51625, will not remove corrosion but will act to assist in
preventing future corrosion. It is acceptable to perform general solvent cleaning
per Clean Bare, Clad, or Plated Metal with Solvent, TASK 20-10-34-110-802 as
an alternative to the products recommended by Grantize.
(b) Remove any dust, dirt, unwanted material, oil, grease or moisture.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-005-F00
(3) Mask the lipskin.
(a) Mask the inner and outer barrel assembly and the fan compartment.
(b) Make sure that the sealant common to the lipskin is protected.
(c) It is permitted for about 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) of the lipskin to be unprotected.
(d) Apply Rulon J tape, G02356, to the three radial seams of the lipskin.
(e) Do not apply the protective coating to the acoustic barrel area.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-005-F00
(4) Prepare for the application of X20-18 compound, G51625, to the lipskin.
(a) Make sure that the lipskin surface temperature is between 67.5 ±22.5°F (19.7 ±12.5°C).
(b) Avoid application of X20-18 compound, G51625, when the ambient humidity is above
90%.
(c) Apply a few drops of the X20-18 compound, G51625, to a soft cotton applicator. Do not
saturate the applicator to the point of dripping.
NOTE: If the X20-18 compound, G51625, pours out in a cloudy or milky consistency, do
not use it. Discard the remaining contents.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-006-F00
(5) Apply X20-18 compound, G51625, to the lipskin.
(a) Apply a thin film of X20-18 compound, G51625, to an area of 2.5 ±0.5 ft 2 (0.2 ±0.0 m 2) in
a sweeping motion.
71-00-03
1) Do not allow the X20-18 compound, G51625, to dry. Wipe the treated area
immediately with a dry and soft cloth until all wet film is buffed off and no longer
visible. Rotate the cloth as necessary when absorbency decreases.
NOTE: The initial application of the X20-18 compound, G51625, may remove
remaining amounts of polishing residue if cleaning wasn't completed
adequately. If only a small amount; proceed with application. Otherwise,
repeat cleaning steps in previous section.
NOTE: Direct exposure to sunlight or warm surface temperatures can result in
streaking.
(b) Repeat application process until entire lipskin is treated. The process is complete when
three (3) coats are applied.
NOTE: The process is complete when three coats are applied.
1) Allow a minimum of 30 minutes between coat applications.
NOTE: X20-18 compound, G51625, has a 12 hour cure time.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-007-F00
(6) It is recommended to repolish and reapply X20-18 compound, G51625, at a cycle of every
ninety (90) days or after the surface loses its shine. Whichever occurs first.
NOTE: Boeing recommends a schedule for checking the lipskin visual appearance every two
(2) weeks for the first two (2) months and then adjusting the schedule according to
operator experience based on environment and use of airplane.
(a) To detect the presence of X20-18 compound, G51625, on bare metal surfaces, perform
one of the following:
1) Use Rulon J tape, G02356, fold one end back to make a tab at the end. Firmly
press the tape on a subject treated area and suspected untreated area. Pull the tab
back slowly at a 90 degree angle to the surface. Noticeable ease in resistance will
take place on a treated surface compared to a non-treated surface.
2) Spray clean deionized water on the surface. Moisture will bead up on a treated
surface when compared to a non-treated surface.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-006-F00
(7) Remove the masking material from the inner and outer barrels and the fan compartment.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-040-002-F00
(8) If engine idle runs will be performed throughout aircraft storage, it is required to deactivate the
engine anti-ice system if X20-18 compound, G51625, is still applied to the lipskin. Deactivating
the engine anti-ice system will allow the X20-18 compound, G51625, to be left on during
engine runs.
NOTE: Failure to keep the Engine Anti Ice deactivated during the entire engine run with AECI
3 applied to the lipskin would cause AECI 3 burning, and will result in permanent
staining of the lipskin.
(a) Make sure that the X20-18 compound, G51625, has cured for 12 hours before performing
engine runs.
(b) Deactivate the engine anti-ice system with the engine anti-ice valve inoperative CLOSED
(TASK 30-00-00-040-803).
NOTE: The system can be left deactivated throughout storage. There is no need to do
the restoration procedure after each engine run.
71-00-03
G. Method 2 - Protective Coating Application
WARNING
MAKE SURE THAT YOU READ THE MANUFACTURER'S SAFETY DATA
SHEET (MSDS) FOR THE MATERIALS YOU WILL USE, AND WEAR THE
PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND EQUIPMENT IF IT IS SPECIFIED. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY , INJURY TO PERSONS CAN OCCUR.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-005-F00
(1) If it is necessary, remove existing pitting, corrosion and surface oxidation from inlet cowl
lipskin.
(a) Use the applicable SRM procedure.
(b) Make sure that the minimum thickness requirements per the SRM are met.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-001-F00
(2) Clean the lipskin and get a water break free surface.
(a) Use a lint-free cloth, G00834, and solvent, B00666, to wipe the lipskin.
(b) Remove any dust, dirt, unwanted material, oil, grease or moisture.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-003-F00
(3) Mask the lipskin.
(a) Mask the inner and outer barrel assembly and the fan compartment.
(b) Make sure that the sealant common to the lipskin is protected.
(c) It is permitted for about 0.1 in. (2.54 mm) of the lipskin to be unprotected.
(d) Apply Rulon J tape, G02356, to the three radial seams of the lipskin.
(e) Do not apply the protective coating to the acoustic barrel area.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-001-F00
(4) Prepare the basecoat Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013.
(a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.1°C) - 80°F (26.7°C).
(b) Mix the material to a homogeneous consistency.
(c) Standard spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and pot
pressure of 5 psi (34.5 kPa) is recommended to get the proper fluid delivery.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-002-F00
(5) Apply the basecoat Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013, to the lipskin.
(a) Apply a 4 mils (0.004 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment.
(b) Let this layer dry for 1 hour.
NOTE: You can decrease this time with warm air or infrared lamps. Protect the area from
freezing.
(c) Apply a second layer to get a total of 8 mils (0.008 in.) thickness.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-003-F00
(6) Prepare the Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014.
(a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.1°C) - 80°F (26.7°C).
(b) Mix the material to a homogeneous consistency.
(c) Apply the topcoat in two separate layers using standard spray equipment with an
atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and pot pressure of 5 psi (34.5 kPa).
71-00-03
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-004-F00
(7) Apply the Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014, to the lipskin.
(a) Make sure that the basecoat is dry (no gloss).
(b) The temperature at the time of application and drying should be a minimum of 40°F
(4.4°C). Protect the area from freezing.
(c) Dry apply the first layer of topcoat over the basecoat with a wide fan and the gun held
about 18 in. (45.7 cm) from the surface.
1) This discontinuous layer should barely cover the black basecoat to minimize
bubbles in the protective coating.
(d) Apply a second layer in a usual spray application to get a thickness of 3 mils (0.003 in.) of
dry film.
(e) The basecoat and topcoat will fully dry together to make a rain resistant coating with
these conditions:
1) Two hours of drying time with conditions of 50% relative humidity and 70°F
(21.1°C).
2) The lipskin can be dried outside if there is no direct rain and the temperature is
about 50°F (10.0°C).
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-008-F00
(8) Prepare the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411.
NOTE: PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, can be used alone or for added exterior durability it can
be over coated with Z6148 preservation topcoat.
(a) Let the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, get to 70°F (21.11°C) – 80°F (26.67°C).
(b) Fully mix the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, in the container.
NOTE: If a mechanical paint shaker is used, the recommended mix time is 5 minutes.
(c) Apply the basecoat with standard spray equipment.
NOTE: Use spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and a pot
pressure of 5 psi (34 kPa) to make sure that the fluid is delivered correctly.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-009-F00
(9) Apply the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, to the lip skin.
(a) Apply a 4 mils (0.004 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment.
(b) Let the first coat dry for one hour.
NOTE: Drying can be accelerated by the circulation of warm air.
(c) Apply a second 4 mils (0.004 in.) layer to achieve a total coating of 8 mils (0.008 in.)
thickness.
(d) Let the second coat dry for one hour.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-010-F00
(10) Prepare the PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412.
(a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.11°C) – 80°F (26.67°C).
(b) Fully mix the PPG Z6160 coating, C50411, in the container.
NOTE: If a mechanical paint shaker is used, the recommended mix time is 5 minutes.
71-00-03
(c) Apply the topcoat with standard spray equipment.
NOTE: Use spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and a pot
pressure of 5 psi (34 kPa) to make sure that the fluid is delivered correctly.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-011-F00
(11) Apply the PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, to the lip skin.
(a) Make sure that the basecoat is dry (no gloss).
(b) Apply a 2 mils (0.002 in.) layer in one application with the spray equipment.
(c) Allow to dry for two hours.
NOTE: Full cure is achieved in 16 hours.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-012-F00
(12) Prepare the Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410.
(a) Let the material get to 70°F (21.11°C) – 80°F (26.67°C).
(b) Fully mix the Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410, in the container.
(c) Apply the coating with standard spray equipment.
NOTE: Use spray equipment with an atomization pressure of 75 psi (517 kPa) and a pot
pressure of 5 psi (34 kPa) to make sure that the fluid is delivered correctly.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-370-013-F00
(13) Apply the Gardo Protect 350 coating, C50410, to the lip skin.
(a) Apply a 2 mils (0.002 in.) - 3 mils (0.003 in.) layer in one application with the spray
equipment.
(b) Allow to dry for 15 to 30 minutes.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-950-004-F00
(14) Remove the masking material from the inner and outer barrels and the fan compartment.
H. Method 3 - Weekly Inspection for Corrosion and Cleaning
SUBTASK 71-00-03-100-004-F00
(1) If a protective coating is not available, do the following at least once (1) weekly. Daily
inspection and cleaning is preferred.
NOTE: Frequency of inspections will depend on the environmental condition that the airplane
is stored in. Inspections and cleaning should be done at a frequency that ensures the
lipskin does not have corrosive substance build up or prolonged moisture pooling on
the lipskin surface.
(a) With a soft low-lint cleaning cloth, G50933, moisten with alcohol, B00130, (preferred) or
with de-ionized water, G02418, clean the nose cowl lipskin (TASK 20-10-34-110-802).
(b) If corrosion is found, remove per the applicable SRM procedure. Make sure that the
minimum thickness requirements per SRM are met.
I. Protective Coating Removal
SUBTASK 71-00-03-000-001-F00
(1) Do one of these steps to remove the protective coating from the lipskin:
(a) If X20-18 compound, G51625, was used, perform the following steps:
71-00-03
1) Clean the lipskin with XS3 Aircraft Wash and XG5 Hard Surface Cleaner furnished
from the X20-18 compound, G51625, vendor.
NOTE: It is acceptable to perform general solvent cleaning per SOPM 20-30-03 as
an alternative to the products recommended by Granitize.
2) Clean the surface until there are no signs of X20-18 compound, G51625, present on
the lipskin.
a) To detect the presence of X20-18 compound, G51625, on bare metal surfaces,
perform one of the following:
<1> Use Rulon J tape, G02356, to make a tab at the end. Firmly press the
tape on a subject treated area and suspected untreated area. Pull the
tab back slowly at a 90 degree angle to the surface. Noticeable ease in
resistance will take place on a treated compared to the untreated
surface.
<2> Spray clean de-ionized water, G02418, on the surface. Moisture will
bead up on a treated surface when compared to a non-treated surface.
3) Do this task if the aircraft will be put back into service: MMEL 30-03 (DDPG)
Restoration - Engine and Nose Cowl Anti-Ice Valves Inoperative,
TASK 30-00-00-440-803.
(b) If Protectapeel SC-1074B-1 coating, C50013/Protectapeel SC-1090 topcoat, C50014,
PPG Z6160 coating, C50411/PPG Z6148 topcoat, C50412, or Gardo Protect 350 coating,
C50410, was used, perform one of the following steps:
1) Use your hand to peel off the coating or use clean shop air.
a) Refer to the coating manufacturer's recommendations for more details.
2) Do not use hand tools harder than the aluminum lipskin to prevent damage.
CAUTION
SCRIBE MARKS OR CUTS WHICH GO INTO THE METAL SURFACE OF
THE LIP SKIN CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE LIP SKIN. THE DAMAGE
CAUSES LOSS OF FATIGUE LIFE OF THE METAL.
(c) If necessary, use a hard resin phenolic scraper, STD-1064, (or equivalent), to help you
remove the peelable coating with these conditions:
1) The tool does not go completely through the coating
2) The tool does not score or mar the lipskin
3) Use a scraper which has an adjustable depth of cut on the coating.
71-00-03-600-802-F00Preservation of An Engine On-Wing (Task Selection)PDF p. 493

4. Preservation of An Engine On-Wing (Task Selection)
A. General
(1) The purpose of this task is to permit you to select the applicable method to do the engine
preservation.
(2) This procedure is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing).
B. Consumable Materials
Reference Description Specification
G02455 [CP2160] Film, Vapor Barrier, Polyethylene L-P-512
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-002-F00
(1) From the time specification for the preservation tasks, select the applicable task to do the
engine preservation:
(a) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than 10 Days (Engine On-Wing),
TASK 71-00-03-600-804-F00.
(b) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing),
TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00.
(c) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than Three Months (Engine
On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-809-F00.
(d) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine From One Month to One Year (Engine On-Wing),
TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-043-F00
(2) These tasks give the instructions for the preservation, preservation renewal and
depreservation for a serviceable and a non-serviceable engine.
NOTE: For this procedure, a serviceable engine is defined as an engine that you can start. A
non-serviceable engine is defined as an engine that cannot be started.
(a) The preservation procedures for a serviceable engine gives the minimum recommended
steps that are necessary to prevent these conditions:
1) Corrosion
2) Entry of unwanted material into the engine
3) The effects of the climate and weather conditions.
(b) The preservation procedures for a non-serviceable engine gives the minimum
recommended steps that are necessary if you cannot start the engine
(c) The preservation renewal procedure, if it is permitted, gives the instructions for the
renewal of the preservation time.
(d) The depreservation procedure puts the installed engine back in operation.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-044-F00
(3) The preservation procedures are different for different periods of non-operational time, different
types of preservation procedures, and if the power plant is serviceable or not serviceable.
71-00-03
(a) Power plant preservation is a flexible program that you can do, and must agree with the
applicable weather and storage conditions.
(b) More care is necessary for a program for power plants that are operational in high
humidity or large temperature changes or near a salt water area, than for the power
plants that are in drier climates or less bad weather conditions.
1) More care is necessary for power plants exposed to contaminants that promote
corrosion (i.e deicing material).
(c) You must do a schedule for the preservation programs for power plants that are not
serviceable to do the preservation renewal procedures and monitor the schedule
regularly to make sure that you did the necessary procedure before the expiration time.
(d) In case of engine storage environmental humidity level that is higher than 70%, put
desiccant bags in position with a humidity indicator in the inlet and the exhaust in order to
monitor the humidity level.
NOTE: The best condition for engine storage is to keep an environment with less than
70% relative humidity.
1) Make sure that the desiccant bags are not in contact with the engine hardware.
2) If necessary, use vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160] to locally protect the engine
hardware.
3) Attach humidity indicator card (locally available) to monitor humidity level during the
preservation period.
4) Make sure desiccant bags and humidity indicators are easily accessible.
(e) When you use desiccants, you must do an inspection of them and change them regularly
as applicable to the environmental conditions.
NOTE: Installation of vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160] in inlet and exhaust can help
to correctly seal engine flow path to make sure of desiccant bags effectiveness.
NOTE: This will make sure that the desiccant gives good protection.
(f) You must close the variable bleed valve (VBV) doors when you do the preservation and
store the power plant.
NOTE: Make sure that no unwanted material goes into the core engine inlet through the
VBV's.
(g) You must do the engine dry-out procedure after an engine had an in-flight shutdown, or
when you do the long term preservation for a not serviceable engine.

Reference Description

tape, G51576, or tape, G00920.

plastic

pillowing of the plastic sheeting.

(14.1 N·m).

9. Preservation Renewal of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing)
A. General
(1) This task is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing).
(2) This task gives the instructions for a serviceable and a non-serviceable power plant.
(3) Before engine operation, refer to TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00 for lipskin coating requirements
during engine operation.
B. References
Reference Title
36-11-02-400-801 Bleed Air Check Valve - Installation (P/B 401)
36-11-04-400-801 PRSOV Installation (P/B 401)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Serviceable Power Plant
SUBTASK 71-00-03-420-005-F00
(1) Before engine operation, if the Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve (PRSOV) and 5th stage
bleed air check valve were removed and stored off the airplane, do the steps that follow:
(a) Remove the coupling, blanking plate, and E-seal from the duct.
(b) Inspect the duct openings for unwanted material.
(c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801.
(d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve -
Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-002-F00
(2) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than One Month (Engine On-Wing),
TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00.
(a) If you do a 30–day preservation with engine idle run, this procedure can be renewed five
(5) more times for a total duration of 180 days (TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00).
(b) If you do a 30-day preservation with engine dry motor, this procedure can be renewed
two (2) more times for a total duration of 90 days (TASK 71-00-03-600-806-F00).
NOTE: During engine idle run, both oil and fuel circulate through its system. During
engine dry motor, the fuel does not circulate through the complete fuel system.
(c) If the power plant will be kept for more than the subsequent 30 days, you must do one of
these steps:
1) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine for Not More Than Three Months (Engine
On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-809-F00.
2) Do the preservation of a serviceable engine from one month to one year
(TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00).
(d) If applicable, apply protective coating to the inlet cowl lipskin after engine operation, do
this task: Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure, TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00.
71-00-03

(c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801.
(d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve -
Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-008-F00
(3) Do the preservation of a not serviceable engine from one month to one year
(TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00).

SUBTASK 71-00-03-210-007-F00
(1) If it is operator policy, examine and clean the IDG air/oil cooler (Reference Not Currently
Available and TASK 24-11-21-200-801).
NOTE: This check is recommended to prevent corrosion and cooler failure especially during
operation in winter.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-680-001-F00
(2) If it is not already done, do this task: Drain the Engine Oil, TASK 12-13-11-600-803.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-009-F00
(3) To fill the oil tank with preservation oil, do this task: Replenish the Engine Oil,
TASK 12-13-11-600-801.
(a) Fill the oil tank with 20 qt (19 l) of one of the preservation oils given below:
1) Engine oil, D00599 [CP2442], and at least 5 percent by volume of oil, D00664
[CP5067], or
2) Engine oil, D00599 [CP2442], and at least 7 percent by volume of additive, D00662
[CP5075].
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-048-F00
(4) Alternative method without oil tank draining: it is possible to skip step (2) above and prepare
the mixture directly if you add the appropriate amount of corrosion preventive oil or corrosion
inhibitor to the oil remaining in the tank.
(a) In this case, add 1 qt (1 l) (resp. 1.4 qt (1.3 l)) of system corrosion preventive oil, D00664
[CP5067] (resp. corrosion preventive additive, D00662 [CP5075]), in the oil tank.
(b) If it is necessary, partially drain the oil tank before you add the additive to prevent over
servicing.
(c) Complete the servicing with engine oil, D00599 [CP2442], after you add the additive.
NOTE: In this case, operating the engine at ground idle (step 5 below) is necessary and
cannot be replaced by dry motoring.
(d) If it is necessary, check oil level.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-860-003-F00
(5) Perform idle run as follows:
(a) Do this task: Start the Engine Procedure (Selection), TASK 71-00-00-800-807-F00.
(b) Let the engine become stable for 15-20 minutes at the idle.
(c) Do this task: Stop the Engine Procedure (Usual Engine Stop),
TASK 71-00-00-700-819-F00.
71-00-03
(d) When the engine cannot be operated at idle condition, dry motor the engine for 5
minutes, do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00.
NOTE: This alternative is possible only if steps 2 and 3 have been completed (oil tank
draining).
(e) Refer to starter limitation to find out the number of dry motoring cycles to make sure of
the total motoring time.
NOTE: Preferred method to preserve the engine is by doing an idle run. During engine
idle run, both oil and fuel circulate through its system. During engine dry motor,
the fuel does not circulate through the complete fuel system.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-710-003-F00
(6) If the VBV doors are open, close them.
(a) Do this task: VBV Actuation System - Manual Operation, TASK 75-32-00-730-801-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-710-004-F00
(7) Put vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], on the VBV bleed grills.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-020-003-F00
(8) If the APU or external air will be used to operate the ECS while the engine is preserved, it is
recommended to remove the PRSOV and 5th stage bleed air check valve and store them off of
the airplane, do these steps:
(a) Remove the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Removal, TASK 36-11-04-000-801.
(b) Remove the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve -
Removal, TASK 36-11-02-000-801.
NOTE: If removal of the fifth stage duct assembly was necessary to remove the bleed air
check valve, it may also be stored off of the airplane.
(c) Install an E-seal and a coupling with a blanking plate, SPL-18258, on the precooler
upstream duct (Figure 206).
1) When the coupling is in place, tighten the coupling.
a) Tighten the coupling nut to 115.0 in-lb (13.0 N·m) - 125.0 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
b) Lightly tap the outer surface of the coupling with a rubber mallet, STD-3906.
c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 115.0 in-lb (13.0 N·m) - 125.0 in-lb
(14.1 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY THE G00920 TAPE TO THE PAINTED SURFACES. THE
TAPE IS HARD TO REMOVE. IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THESE
SURFACES.
(d) On the intersection manifold duct assembly and fifth stage duct assembly, cover the
openings with a protective cover or use a barrier (plastic sheet) and tape.
(e) Make the barrier from barrier material, G00253, polyethylene film, G00252, or an
equivalent 6 MIL or thicker material.
(f) Use the preferred 3M 8979 tape, G51663, or 3M 8979N tape, G51664, or alternate tape,
G51576, or tape, G00920.
1) If the fifth stage duct assembly is removed during removal of the bleed air check

SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-009-F00

2) If not possible, as an alternative, install the kit, COM-1501 (preferred), or inlet cover,

H. Overdue Situation
SUBTASK 71-00-03-550-003-F00
(1) Up to three months of overdue are permitted without additional maintenance before return to
service or preservation renewal, only if:
NOTE: The following overdue extension is not intended to be used routinely.
NOTE: The maximum expiration period of three months is permitted only one time in the full
duration of the engine storage period (with renewals included) before return to service.
(a) The engine is stored with engine covers installed (or equivalent specified in the AMM
preservation procedure).
(b) The engine is stored in an indoor location (hanger) with controlled environment, the
humidity level must be kept below 70%:
1) With the hangar conditioning system.
2) With the installation and monitoring of desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098].
(c) The storage complies with the requirements of these tasks: Preservation of an Engine for
Not More Than Three Months (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-809-F00 and
Preservation of An Engine On-Wing (T ask Selection), TASK 71-00-03-600-802-F00.
(d) The fuel system was not drained during the storage period.

[CP2160], and desiccant bag, G02456 [CP2098].
(a) Make sure that you remove all of the moisture barrier tape, G02304, from the inlet and
exhaust areas and that there is no unwanted material.
(b) Make sure that you remove all vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], from the Variable
Bleed Valve (VBV) bleed grills.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-630-006-F00
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT YOU FOLLOW THE LIPSKIN COATING PROCEDURES
BEFORE AN ENGINE OPERATION. IF YOU DO NOT FOLLOW
INSTRUCTIONS, THE COATING CAN MELT AND GO INTO THE ENGINE.
THIS CAN CAUSE ENGINE DAMAGE.
(2) If not already done, remove the lipskin protective coating from the inlet cowl lipskin
(TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00).
SUBTASK 71-00-03-420-002-F00
(3) If the PRSOV and 5th stage bleed air check valve were removed and stored off the airplane,
do the steps that follow:
(a) Remove the coupling, blanking plate, and E-seal from the duct.
(b) Inspect the duct openings for unwanted material.
(c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801.
(d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve -
Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-680-005-F00
(4) Do this task: Drain the Engine Oil, TASK 12-13-11-600-803.
(a) Make sure that you drain the oil tank and the accessory gearbox.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-680-006-F00
(5) Do this task: Starter Servicing (Oil Drain), TASK 80-11-01-680-801-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-610-004-F00
(6) Do a check of the oil tank level.
(a) If it is necessary to fill the tank, do this task: Replenish the Engine Oil,
TASK 12-13-11-600-801.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-610-005-F00
(7) Do this task: Starter Servicing (Oil Fill), TASK 80-11-01-610-801-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-790-003-F00
(8) Do this task: Wet Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-822-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-790-004-F00
(9) Do this task: Test 3A - Idle-Power Leak Check, TASK 71-00-00-700-801-F00.
(a) Operate the engine at idle for ten minutes before you stop the engine.

G. Power Plant Preservation (Serviceable)
SUBTASK 71-00-03-910-003-F00
(1) Obey the CAUTIONS when you do this procedure:
CAUTION
DO NOT SPRAY PRESERVATIVE OIL INTO ENGINE GAS PATH, AS
POSSIBLE DIRT DEPOSITION ON BLADES AND VANES WILL REDUCE
ENGINE EFFICIENCY .
CAUTION
DO NOT SPRAY PRESERVATIVE OIL OR EQUIVALENT INTO THE
ENGINE INLET , CORE COMPRESSOR, TURBINE, OR ENGINE
EXHAUST . UNWANTED PARTICLES THAT STAY ON THE BLADES AND
VANES WET WITH OIL CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE.
CAUTION
DO NOT USE SILICONE-BASED OILS IN THE FUEL SYSTEM. THIS WILL
HELP PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM.
(a) Do not apply a spray of preservative oil into the inlet, compressor, turbine, or exhaust.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-050-F00
(2) If it is operator policy, examine and clean the Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) air/oil cooler
(Reference Not Currently Available and TASK 24-11-21-200-801).
NOTE: This check is recommended to prevent corrosion and cooler failure especially during
operation in winter.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-680-002-F00
(3) If it is not already done, do this task: Drain the Engine Oil, TASK 12-13-11-600-803.
71-00-03
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-012-F00
(4) To fill the oil tank with preservative oil, do this task: Replenish the Engine Oil,
TASK 12-13-11-600-801.
NOTE: This step may be done just before the last ground run/flight.
NOTE: Only oil, D00664 [CP5067], is approved by the engine manufacturer to be used to
operate the engine just before the last ground run/flight.
(a) Fill the oil tank with 20 qt (19 l) of one of the preservative oils given below:
1) oil, D00599 [CP2442], and at least 5 percent by volume of oil, D00664 [CP5067]
(CP2851), or
2) oil, D00599 [CP2442], and at least 7 percent by volume of additive, D00662
[CP5075].
SUBTASK 71-00-03-860-005-F00
(5) Perform idle run as follows:
(a) Do this task: Start the Engine Procedure (Selection), TASK 71-00-00-800-807-F00.
(b) Let the engine become stable for 15-20 minutes at the idle.
1) When the engine cannot be operated at idle condition, dry motor the engine for 4
minutes, do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00.
(c) Do this task: Stop the Engine Procedure (Usual Engine Stop),
TASK 71-00-00-700-819-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-010-F00
(6) If you remove an engine component, make sure that you install protective covers and gaskets
on all openings.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-013-F00
(7) Do these steps to do the engine fuel system preservation:
(a) Make sure that the applicable engine start lever is in the CUTOFF position.
1) Install the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the applicable engine start lever.
(b) Make sure that the SPAR VALVE CLOSED light, on the P5 overhead panel, is dim.
NOTE: The light for the engine spar valve has three positions: 1) bright when the valve is
in transition or when it does not agree with the commanded position; or 2) dim
when the valve is closed; or 3) OFF when the valve is opened.
(c) Do these steps to drain the fuel supply line (Figure 207):
1) Put the 5-gallon (19-liter) fuel resistant container, STD-1054, below the fuel filter
drain plug [22].
2) Remove the drain plug [22] and let the fuel drain.
NOTE: The drain plug has a 13/16-inch fitting.
3) Remove and discard the O-ring [21] from the drain plug [22].
4) Lubricate a new O-ring [21] with vaseline, D00672 [CP5070], or oil, D00623
[CP5066], and install it on the drain plug [22].
5) Lubricate the threads of the drain plug [22] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601
[CP2101].
6) Install the drain plug [22].
a) Tighten the drain plug [22] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).
71-00-03
7) Attach safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006], to the
drain plug [22].
(d) Disconnect the fuel inlet line at the engine fuel tube (Figure 208).
1) Remove the bolts [31] that attach the fuel inlet line to the engine fuel tube.
2) Remove the gasket [32] from the fuel inlet line.
a) Keep the gasket [32] for the later installation.
3) Install a protective cover on the fuel inlet line.
(e) Connect a temporary line from the engine oil servicing dispenser, COM-1537, to the
engine fuel tube to supply oil, D00623 [CP5066], at 50 psi (345 kPa) maximum pressure.
1) If a pressurized oil cart is not available, a 42 qt (40 l) gravity flow container is
permitted if the container is 1 ft (305 mm) above the fuel pump.
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO TIGHTEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUTS. USE
ONE TO HOLD THE MATING PART , AND THE OTHER TO TIGHTEN THE
COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO
THE TUBES AND MATING PART CAN OCCUR.
(f) Disconnect the line from the PCR port on the Hydro-Mechanical Unit (HMU).
(g) Install a temporary hose drain line 118 in. (3 m) long from the PCR port on the HMU and
put the other end of the hose in a oil resistant container (10 gal), STD-3938.
1) Attach the end of the hose to the container to prevent fluid leakage.
(h) If the oil cart is used, apply and hold an oil pressure of 50 psi (345 kPa) maximum to the
fuel pump inlet.
1) Hold this pressure during the motoring of the engine.
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY BOOST PUMP PRESSURE TO THE FUEL PUMP INLET
WHEN YOU DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE WITH THE DISCONNECTED
FUEL LINE. FUEL WILL SPILL ON THE ENGINE AND CAUSE DAMAGE
TO THE EQUIPMENT .
(i) Do this task: Dry Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-821-F00.
CAUTION
DO NOT CONTINUE TO DRY-MOTOR THE ENGINE WITHOUT
PRESERVATIVE FLUID IN THE GRAVITY FLOW CONTAINER. IF
YOU DO, DAMAGE TO THE FUEL PUMP CAN OCCUR.
1) Cease dry motoring operation after visual verification of preservative fluid leaving
HMU is observed.
(j) After the engine stops, remove the temporary drain line from the PCR port on the HMU.
(k) Do these steps to tighten the coupling nut:
1) Install the PCR line to the PCR port.
CAUTION
USE TWO WRENCHES TO TIGHTEN THE TUBE COUPLING NUTS.
USE ONE TO HOLD THE MATING PART , AND THE OTHER TO
TIGHTEN THE COUPLING NUT . IF YOU DO NOT USE TWO
WRENCHES, DAMAGE TO THE TUBES AND MATING PART CAN
OCCUR.
2) Tighten the coupling nut to 285 ±15 in-lb (32.2 ±1.7 N·m).
71-00-03
(l) Do these steps to let the preservation fluid flow in the engine:
1) Make sure to do this check of the circuit breakers before you do the wet motor
procedure to prevent fuel leakage.
2) Open these circuit breakers and install safety tags:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
B 3 C00360 FUEL SPAR VALVE ENG 2
B 4 C00359 FUEL SPAR VALVE ENG 1
3) Remove the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, from the applicable engine start
lever.
4) Do this task: Wet Motor the Engine, TASK 71-00-00-700-822-F00.
5) Wet motor the engine for 5 seconds or until you see a spray of the preservation fluid
out the engine exhaust nozzle.
6) Move the engine start lever to the CUTOFF position and continue to motor for 2
minutes.
a) Install the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the applicable engine start
lever.
7) Put the applicable engine start switch to the CONT position.
NOTE: When you stop the engine with the engine start switch in the CONT
position, the Electronic Engine Control (EEC) will command the Variable
Stator Vane (VSV)'s to the full open position and the Variable Bleed Valve
(VBV)'s to the full closed position.
8) Let the engine stop completely.
9) Put the applicable engine start switch to the OFF position.
10) Remove the safety tags and close these circuit breakers:
F/O Electrical System Panel, P6-3
Row Col Number Name
B 3 C00360 FUEL SPAR VALVE ENG 2
B 4 C00359 FUEL SPAR VALVE ENG 1
(m) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.
(n) Remove the temporary oil supply line from the engine fuel tube.
(o) Do this step to make sure that the gasket [32] is clean and serviceable:
1) Do this task: Seals (Preformed Packings and O-Rings) and Gaskets,
TASK 70-30-01-910-802-F00.
(p) Lubricate the threads of the bolts [31] with Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006.
(q) Install the bolts [31] to attach the fuel inlet line to the engine fuel tube.
(r) Tighten the bolts [31] to 50 in-lb (5.6 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).
SUBTASK 71-00-03-020-006-F00
(8) If the Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) or external air will be used to operate the Environmental
Control System (ECS) while the engine is preserved, it is recommended to remove the PRSOV
and 5th stage bleed air check valve and store them off of the airplane, do these steps:
(a) Remove the Pressure Regulating and Shutoff Valve (PRSOV), do this task: PRSOV
Removal, TASK 36-11-04-000-801.
71-00-03
(b) Remove the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve -
Removal, TASK 36-11-02-000-801.
NOTE: If removal of the fifth stage duct assembly was necessary to remove the bleed air
check valve, it may also be stored off airplane.
(c) Install an E-seal and a coupling with the blanking plate, SPL-18258, on the precooler
upstream duct (Figure 206).
1) When the coupling is in place, tighten the coupling.
a) Tighten the coupling nut to 115.0 in-lb (13.0 N·m) - 125.0 in-lb (14.1 N·m).
b) Lightly tap the outer surface of the coupling with the rubber mallet, STD-3906.
c) Tighten the coupling nut again to 115.0 in-lb (13.0 N·m) - 125.0 in-lb
(14.1 N·m).
CAUTION
DO NOT APPLY THE G00920 TAPE TO THE PAINTED SURFACES. THE
TAPE IS HARD TO REMOVE. IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THESE
SURFACES.
(d) On the intersection manifold duct assembly and fifth stage duct assembly, cover the
openings with a protective cover or use a barrier (plastic sheet) and tape.
(e) Make the barrier from barrier material, G00253, polyethylene film, G00252, or an
equivalent 6 MIL or thicker material.
(f) Use the preferred 3M 8979 tape, G51663, or 3M 8979N tape, G51664, or alternate tape,
G51576, or tape, G00920.
1) If the fifth stage duct assembly is removed during removal of the bleed air check
valve, cover the opening on the engine case (fifth stage port) with a barrier (plastic
sheet) and tape.
2) Make the barrier from barrier material, G00253, polyethylene film, G00252, or an
equivalent 6 MIL or thicker material.
3) Use the preferred 3M 8979 tape, G51663, 3M 8979N tape, G51664, or alternate
tape, G51576, or tape, G00920.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-980-002-F00
(9) If the VBV doors are open, close them, do this task: VBV Actuation System - Manual
Operation, TASK 75-32-00-730-801-F00.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-011-F00
(10) Put vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], on the VBV bleed grills.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-012-F00
(11) Install protective covers on all disconnected lines and electrical connections.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-039-F00
(12) Put desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098], and humidity indicators in the inlet and exhausts of the
engine to protect it from moisture as follows:
NOTE: Desiccant bags must be inspected/replaced at regular intervals depending on weather
conditions.
(a) Make sure that they are accessible for inspection/replacement while disturbing a
minimum amount of protective material, do this task: Desiccant Bags Inspection
Procedure, TASK 71-00-03-200-801-F00.
(b) Mark the date on the humidity indicator tags.
71-00-03
(c) Attach desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098], in the inlet and exhausts of the engine.
1) Make sure that they are not in contact with the engine hardware.
(d) If necessary, use vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], to locally protect the engine
hardware.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-013-F00
(13) Seal the inlet and exhaust openings with the vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160].
(a) Attach vapor barrier film, G02455 [CP2160], with moisture barrier tape, G02304.
(b) To cover the inlet opening, apply the tape at the inner barrel ring (Figure 205).
(c) Do not apply tape to or on the inlet cowl lipskin.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-480-016-F00
(14) Put the adequate protective cover that follows:
(a) If the engine is stored on-wing, put a waterproof cover over the whole powerplant.
1) Make sure that it is tightly fitted to the powerplant.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE THAT THE DRAIN MASTS ARE CLEAR OF BLOCKAGE.
BLOCKED DRAINS CAN CAUSE WATER TO COLLECT IN THE
THRUST REVERSER. THIS CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
EQUIPMENT .
2) If not possible, as an alternative, install the kit, COM-1501 (preferred), or inlet cover,
COM-1516, and exhaust plug, SPL-18121 (alternate), to prevent fan windmilling
and to prevent Foreign Object Damage (FOD).
NOTE: The exhaust plug, SPL-18121, installs to the exhaust and bypass of the
engine.

(2) Do these steps to prepare for the procedure:
(a) Make sure that the applicable engine start lever is in the CUTOFF position.
1) Install the DO NOT OPERATE tag, STD-858, on the applicable engine start lever.
(b) Make sure that the SPAR VALVE CLOSED light, on the P5 on the overhead panel, is dim.
NOTE: The light for the engine spar valve has three positions: 1) bright when the valve is
in transition or when it does not agree with the commanded position; or 2) dim
when the valve is closed; or 3) OFF when the valve is opened.
(c) Do this task: Remove Electrical Power, TASK 24-22-00-860-812.

(3) Do these steps to drain the fuel system (Figure 207):
(a) Put the 5-gallon (19-liter) fuel resistant container, STD-1054, below the fuel pump.
(b) Disconnect the filter upstream pressure sensing tube from the fuel pump housing.
NOTE: The filter upstream pressure sensing tube is the lower sensing tube. The other
end of this tube is connected to the fuel filter differential pressure switch.
1) Let the fuel drain into the container.
(c) Remove the drain plug [22] and let the fuel drain.
NOTE: The drain plug has a 13/16-inch fitting.
(d) Remove and discard the O-ring [21] from the drain plug [22].
(e) Lubricate a new O-ring [21] with vaseline, D00672 [CP5070], or oil, D00623 [CP5066],
and install it on the drain plug [22].
(f) Lubricate the threads of the drain plug [22] with graphite mineral vaseline, D00601
[CP2101].
(g) Install the drain plug [22].
1) Tighten the drain plug [22] to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).
71-00-03
(h) Attach safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006], to the drain
plug [22].

1) Keep the gasket [32] for the subsequent installation.
2) Install a protective cover on the engine fuel tube.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-010-002-F00

(a) Remove the lube flow screen assembly [23] from the fuel pump, and drain the fuel into

(b) Remove and discard the preformed packing [24] and packing [25] from the screen
assembly.
(c) Lightly lubricate the new packing [24] and packing [25] with oil, D00599 [CP2442].
(d) Install the new packings on the lube flow screen assembly.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-010-003-F00
(6) Remove the fuel filter, do this task: Fuel Filter - Removal, TASK 73-11-02-000-801-F00.

(7) Do these steps to pump preservative oil into the lube flow screen port on the fuel pump:
CAUTION
DO NOT USE SILICONE-BASED OILS IN THE FUEL SYSTEM. THIS WILL
HELP PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE FUEL SYSTEM.
(a) Connect a temporary line from the engine oil servicing dispenser, COM-1537, to the lube
flow screen port to supply oil, D00623 [CP5066], at 50 psi (345 kPa) maximum pressure.
1) Make sure that the oil cart has a 10 micron filter.
2) Tighten the connector to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).
(b) Pump filtered oil into the lube flow screen port until oil flows from the filter upstream
pressure sensing port and the fuel filter housing.
1) Continue to pump oil into the port until no fuel is mixed with the oil.
(c) Connect the filter upstream pressure sensing tube to the fuel pump housing.
1) Tighten the connector to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).
(d) Install a new fuel filter, do this task: Fuel Filter - Installation, TASK 73-11-02-400-801-F00.
(e) Remove the PHP plug [26] from the fuel pump.
(f) Pump filtered oil into the lube flow screen port until oil flows from the PHP port.
1) Continue to pump oil into the port until no fuel is mixed with the oil.
(g) Disconnect the oil cart from the lube flow screen port.
(h) Install the lube flow screen assembly [23] with the new packing [24] and packing [25] in
the fuel pump.
1) Tighten the lube flow screen assembly to 90 in-lb (10.2 N·m) - 110 in-lb (12.4 N·m).
71-00-03
2) Install safety wire, G02345 [CP8001], or safety cable, G50065 [CP8006], to the lube
flow screen assembly.

1) Tighten the connector to 45 in-lb (5.1 N·m) - 55 in-lb (6.2 N·m).

(c) Disconnect the J6 electrical connector from the receptacle identified as CH B on the
HMU.
(d) If it is necessary, use soft nose pliers.
1) Connect the unit, SPL-2178, to the HMU receptacle identified as CH B.

1) Tighten the PCR hose coupling to 180 in-lb (20.3 N·m) - 220 in-lb (24.9 N·m).

I. Overdue Situation
SUBTASK 71-00-03-550-004-F00
(1) Up to three months of overdue are permitted without additional maintenance before return to
service or preservation renewal, only if:
NOTE: The following overdue extension is not intended to be used routinely.
NOTE: The maximum expiration period of three months is permitted only one time in the full
duration of the engine storage period (with renewals included) before return to service.
(a) The engine is stored with engine covers installed (or equivalent specified in the Airplane
Maintenance Manual (AMM) preservation procedure).
(b) The engine is stored in an indoor location (hanger) with controlled environment, the
humidity level must be kept below 70%:
1) With the hangar conditioning system.
2) With the installation and monitoring of desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098].
(c) The storage complies with the requirements of these tasks: Preservation of an Engine
From One Month to One Year (Engine On-Wing), TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00 and
Preservation of An Engine On-Wing (T ask Selection), TASK 71-00-03-600-802-F00.
(d) The fuel system was not drained during the storage period.

15. Preservation Renewal of an Engine From One Month to Not More Than One Year (Engine On-Wing)
A. General
(1) This task is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing).
(2) This task gives the instructions for a serviceable or a non-serviceable power plant.
(3) There is no limit on the number of times you can do this task.
(4) Before engine operation, refer to Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure,
TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00 for lipskin coating requirements during engine operation.
B. References
Reference Title
36-11-02-400-801 Bleed Air Check Valve - Installation (P/B 401)
36-11-04-400-801 PRSOV Installation (P/B 401)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Serviceable Power Plant
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-016-F00
(1) Do this task: Preservation of an Engine From One Month to One Year (Engine On-Wing),
TASK 71-00-03-600-811-F00.
(a) Operate the engine.
1) Before engine operation, if the PRSOV and 5th stage bleed air check valve were
removed and stored off the airplane, do the steps that follow:
a) Remove the coupling, blanking plate, and E-seal from the duct.
b) Inspect the duct openings for unwanted material.
c) Install the PRSOV, do this task: PRSOV Installation, TASK 36-11-04-400-801.
d) Install the 5th stage bleed air check valve, do this task: Bleed Air Check Valve
- Installation, TASK 36-11-02-400-801.
2) After engine operation, if necessary, apply protective coating to the inlet cowl
lipskin, do this task: Inlet Cowl Lipskin Protective Coating Procedure,
TASK 71-00-03-600-815-F00.
E. Not Serviceable Power Plant
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-017-F00
(1) A preservation renewal procedure is not permitted.
(a) You must make the power plant serviceable and do the preservation procedure for a
serviceable power plant before 365 days preservation time is expired.

(12) Do this task: Test 3A - Idle-Power Leak Check, TASK 71-00-00-700-801-F00.
(a) Operate the engine at idle for 10 minutes before you stop the engine.

17. Preservation of an Engine for More Than the One Year Preservation Time Limit (Engine On-Wing)
A. General
(1) This procedure is used for an engine that is installed on the airplane (on-wing).
(2) This procedure is for a power plant that remained preserved for more than the long term
preservation time limit (365 days).
B. Location Zones
Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
71-00-03
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-018-F00
(1) If the engine preservation period of 365 days expired, please refer to your CFM representative
for instructions.
NOTE: Engineering analysis must be used to evaluate the situation. Several factors must be
analyzed: the total time beyond the preservation time limit, the engine storage location
(outside or inside), the humidity level, the temperature changes, how often the
desiccant was changed, and other factors.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-620-026-F00
(2) If the preservation period of 365 days expires on the inlet cowl lipskin, do these steps:
(a) Remove the protective coating on the lipskin.
(b) Examine the lipskin for signs of corrosion.
(c) If it is necessary, you can re-apply the protective coating to preserve the lipskin for
another 365 days.
71-00-03-200-801-F00Desiccant Bags Inspection ProcedurePDF p. 544
Open original AMM PDF - page 544 ↗ 
18. Desiccant Bags Inspection Procedure
A. General
(1) This inspection procedure is to be done if desiccant bags and humidity indicators have been
placed in the inlet and exhaust of the engine.
(2) When you use desiccants, you must examine and change them regularly, as applicable. As an
example, start to monitor the desiccant bags as follows. That will help get a good interval for
desiccant bags replacement. The schedule is as follows:
(a) Second day after storage.
(b) Fourteenth day after storage.
(c) Every three months.
NOTE: The best condition for engine storage is to keep an environment with less than 70
percent of humidity.
B. Consumable Materials
Reference Description Specification
G02456 [CP2098] Desiccant - Activated, Bagged, Packaging Use
And Static Dehumidification
MIL-D-3464
C. Procedure
SUBTASK 71-00-03-010-004-F00
(1) Remove cover and protective material as necessary to get access to humidity indicators.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-210-008-F00
(2) Make sure that you can see the humidity indication at the inlet and exhaust of the engine to
monitor flow path humidity levels.
SUBTASK 71-00-03-200-001-F00
(3) Do a check of the humidity indicators. Their color must show a relative humidity of less than 70
percent. If not, do as follows:
(a) Open the plastic film cover.
71-00-03
(b) Remove, discard and replace desiccant bags, G02456 [CP2098] and humidity indicators
with new ones.
(c) Put protection material and cover back in place.

BASE ASSEMBLY IS NOT MORE THAN 3 MPH (5 KPH) ON A SMOOTH
AND HORIZONTAL SURFACE, OR ENGINE DAMAGE CAN OCCUR.

(c) Move the inlet cowl [31] forward and away from the engine attach flange.
(d) Loosen the lever hoists [34] and turn the inlet cowl [31] until the inlet attach flange faces
down and inlet lip skin faces upward.
(e) Install the inlet cowl [31] on a pallet or other suitable surface.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-900-001-F00
(9) Remove the seal [3] from the forward flange of the inlet cowl TAI duct [1].
(a) Make sure that the seal is serviceable.
(b) If the seal is not serviceable, replace it.
(c) Install the seal.
NOTE: The seal is slightly "oval" and will snap into its position.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-020-007-F00
(10) Install protective caps on the EEC cooling hose [4], inlet cowl TAI duct [1] and openings on the
inlet cowl bulkhead.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-080-002-F00
(11) Remove the sling and overhead hoist as follows:
(a) Release the tension from the straps and lever hoists.
(b) Remove the four hoist pins [33] that attach the inlet cowl sling straps [32] to the inlet
cowl [31].
(c) Remove the sling from the inlet cowl [31].
SUBTASK 71-11-01-980-001-F00
(12) Remove the inlet cowl [31] from the work area.

5. Install the Inlet Cowl (Sling and Overhead Hoist)
(Figure 401, Figure 402, Figure 403)
A. General

(2) This task can be used for the left or right inlet cowl.

6. Remove the Inlet Cowl (Nose Cowl Dolly or Boom Hoist)
(Figure 401, Figure 403, Figure 404, Figure 405)
A. General
(1) The removal and installation of the inlet cowl is done with a nose cowl dolly or a boom hoist.
(a) An overhead hoist is not necessary for this procedure.
(b) The dolly, COM-2060, operates as follows:
1) The dolly is a fixture which has a structural base mounted on three casters.
2) The three casters let the dolly move in the longitudinal direction.
3) Three hand jacks let the dolly move in the vertical direction.
4) For this procedure the nose cowl dolly will be referred to as the dolly.
(c) The boom hoist, SPL-2430, is a boom hoist and uses a installation/removal frame
equipment, SPL-2165, frame assembly to attach to the inlet cowl.
1) The boom hoist is also used for removal of the thrust reverser and aft fairing.

2. Inlet Cowl Inspection
(Figure 601)
A. General
(1) This task examines the skin of the inlet cowl for damage.
B. References
Reference Title
71-11-01-300-801-F01 Replace the Thermal Anti-Ice (TAI) Exhaust Duct (P/B 801)
SRM 54-10-01 Structural Repair Manual
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
412 Engine 1 - Nose Inlet Cowl
422 Engine 2 - Nose Inlet Cowl
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 71-11-01-210-001-F00
(1) Examine the internal skin, the external skin and the lip skin of the inlet cowl for the damage
that follows:
(a) Cracks
(b) Nicks, gouges, scratches and corrosion
(c) Dents
(d) Holes
(e) Erosion (on the lip skin)
(f) Missing sealant between the lip skin segments (3 locations)
1) Missing sealant is permitted between the segments. It is not necessary to re-apply
the sealant.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-220-001-F00
(2) If you find damage, refer to this reference (SRM 54-10-01) for the permitted limits.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-210-004-F00
(3) If you find blockage in the acoustic panel holes in the inner barrel, use the limits for acoustic
area loss (Figure 602)
(a) Acoustic area loss is usually counted when more than half the holes in an area are
blocked and the area is more than one square inch (6.45 square cm).
1) Holes are counted as blocked if fully or not fully filled with adhesive, resin, fibers,
paint or other material.
71-11-01
2) Holes which are angled but are otherwise clear are permitted and not considered
blocked.
3) Some small areas of perforation blockage are part of the new part production
bonding process.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-210-003-F00
(4) Visually examine the cowl Thermal Anti-Ice (TAI) duct louver for signs of cracks or missing
louvers.
NOTE: The TAI duct louver is found at the 6 o'clock position of the inlet cowl.
NOTE: To repair the TAI exhaust duct, remove the duct from the inlet cowl. Do this task:
Replace the Thermal Anti-Ice (TAI) Exhaust Duct, TASK 71-11-01-300-801-F01. It is
not necessary to remove the inlet cowl to do this repair.
(a) If one or more missing louvers are found with no cracks in the slotted areas, it is
permitted to return the airplane to service.
1) Missing louvers should be repaired in 800 hrs after you note the missing louvers.
(b) If one or more missing louvers are found with cracks in the slotted areas, it is permitted to
return the airplane to service with these conditions:
1) If cracks are found in the slotted areas but do not exceed 1 in. (25.40 mm) in length,
do these steps for a temporary repair:
a) Do a stop drill repair with a #30 drill (0.1285 inch dia.) at the end of the cracks.
b) Return the airplane to service.
2) Cracks should be repaired in 800 hrs after you do the temporary repair.
a) Refer to component manual for the applicable repair.
3) If the crack damage is more than 1 in. (25.40 mm) in length in any slot area, the
duct should be replaced or contact the vendor (Goodrich) for disposition.

4. Inlet Cowl Inner Surface Inspection
(Figure 603)
NOTE: This procedure is a scheduled maintenance task.
A. General
(1) This task examines the inner surface skin of the inlet cowl for damage.
B. References
Reference Title
SRM 54-10-01 Structural Repair Manual
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
412 Engine 1 - Nose Inlet Cowl
422 Engine 2 - Nose Inlet Cowl
71-11-01
D. Procedure
SUBTASK 71-11-01-210-005-F00
(1) Examine the internal skin of the inlet cowl for the damage that follows:
(a) Cracks
(b) Nicks, gouges, scratches and corrosion
(c) Dents
(d) Holes
SUBTASK 71-11-01-210-006-F00
(2) If you find damage, refer to this reference (SRM 54-10-01) for the permitted limits.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-220-002-F00
(3) If you find blockage in the acoustic panel holes in the inner barrel, use the limits for acoustic
area loss (Figure 604).
(a) Acoustic area loss is usually counted when more than half the holes in an area are
blocked and the area is more than one square inch (6.45 square cm).
1) Holes are counted as blocked if fully or not fully filled with adhesive, resin, fibers,
paint or other material.
2) Holes which are angled but are otherwise clear are permitted and not considered
blocked.
3) Some small areas of perforation blockage are part of the new part production
bonding process.

A. General
(1) This task is to replace the TAI exhaust duct in the inlet cowl.
(2) Use this procedure for the left or right inlet cowl.
(3) The TAI exhaust duct is found at the 6 o'clock position on the inlet cowl.
B. References
Reference Title
SRM 51-10-01 Structural Repair Manual
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
412 Engine 1 - Nose Inlet Cowl
422 Engine 2 - Nose Inlet Cowl
D. Replace the Thermal Anti-Ice (TAI) Exhaust Duct
SUBTASK 71-11-01-010-003-F01
(1) Do these steps to remove the access panel:
(a) Remove the bolts that attach the access panel to the outer barrel of the inlet cowl.
(b) Remove the access panel.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-020-019-F01
(2) Do these steps to remove the TAI exhaust duct [1]:
(a) Remove the bolts and washers from the flange of the TAI exhaust duct.
(b) Remove the TAI exhaust duct.
(c) Apply tape to cover the TAI duct area on the “D” duct bulkhead of the inlet cowl.
SUBTASK 71-11-01-420-015-F01
(3) Do these steps to install the TAI exhaust duct [1]:
(a) Remove the tape from the TAI duct area.
(b) Put the TAI exhaust duct in the correct position in the inlet cowl.
1) Align the holes in the duct flange with the holes in the inner barrel.
(c) Install the bolts and washers.
1) Tighten the bolts to 30 in-lb (3.39 N·m) - 35 in-lb (3.95 N·m).
SUBTASK 71-11-01-410-008-F01
(4) Do these steps to install the access panel:
NOTE: Make sure you do not damage the bulb seal when you install the access panel.
Carefully guide the exhaust duct stand-off over the TAI duct mounting flange.
(a) Install the access panel with the bulb seal in contact with the flange of the TAI exhaust
duct.
(b) Install the bolts.
71-11-01
1) Tighten the bolts in an alternate pattern to 24 in-lb (2.71 N·m) - 27 in-lb (3.05 N·m).
(c) Apply the aerodynamic sealant to the access panel per SRM 51-10-01.

2. Open the Fan Cowl Panels
(Figure 201)
A. General
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to open the fan cowl panels.
(2) Each fan cowl panel is held open with two hold-open rods.
(3) The hold-open rod is spring-loaded in the stowed position and has a double action lock.
(a) You must pull back the end sleeve and compress the rod from the end to release the
hold-open rod from the stow receiver.
(4) Two clear movements of the lock are necessary to release the hold-open rod from the locked
position.
(a) You must turn and pull the release sleeve in the direction of the arrow.
(b) The hold-open rod is free to extend or compress.

(b) Manually hold the fan cowl panel and move it away from the engine until you can get
access to hold open rods
(c) Do these steps to engage the forward hold-open rod on the engine:
1) Retract the sleeve at the receiver end of the hold-open rod and compress it to
disengage the rod from the receiver.
2) The rod will extend and snap into the first position to hold the fan cowl panel in the
28-degree open position.
71-11-02
3) Engage the hold-open rod on the engine mounted receiver.
NOTE: For the left side of the fan case, the forward receiver is on the engine flange
B1 at the 10:00 o'clock position. The aft receiver is near the fuel nozzle
filter. For the right side of the fan case, the forward receiver is on the engine
flange A1 at the 2:00 o'clock position. The aft receiver is on the flange B6,
aft of the EEC.
(d) Do the steps again, to engage the aft hold-open rod on the engine.
(e) Do these steps to fully open the fan cowl panel to the 55-degree position:
1) Hold the fan cowl panel.
2) Move the TURN/PULL sleeve in the direction of the arrow to unlock each hold-open
rod.
3) Move the fan cowl panel away from the engine until the hold-open rods extend and
snap into the fully open position.

WARNING
DO NOT CLOSE THE FAN COWL PANEL DURING AN ENGINE OPERATION.
THE FORWARD LATCHES ARE IN THE HAZARD AREA ZONE OF THE
ENGINE INLET . IF YOU GO INTO THE HAZARD AREA, YOU CAN GET
PULLED INTO THE ENGINE. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DANGEROUS INJURY
OR DEATH CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU CLOSE THE FAN COWL PANEL IN HIGH WINDS
OR SUDDEN STRONG WIND CONDITIONS. IF YOU DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE
TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
DO NOT TRY TO CLOSE THE FAN COWL IN WINDS MORE THAN 40 KNOTS.
THE FAN COWL PANELS CAN STAY OPEN IN WINDS TO 65 KNOTS. IN
WINDS MORE THAN 65 KNOTS, THE HOLD-OPEN ROD CAN BREAK. IF YOU
DO NOT OBEY , DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT AND INJURY TO PERSONNEL
CAN OCCUR.
WARNING
HOLD THE FAN COWL PANEL WHILE YOU UNLOCK OR RETRACT THE
HOLD-OPEN RODS. IF THE FAN COWL PANEL FALLS, INJURY TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE COMPONENTS CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to engage the hold-open rod on the fan cowl panel:
(a) Hold the fan cowl panel.
(b) Move the TURN/PULL sleeve in the direction of the arrow to unlock each hold-open rod.
(c) Manually move the fan cowl panel toward the engine until the hold-open rods lock at the
first click (28-degree position).
(d) Do these steps to engage the forward hold-open rod on the fan cowl panel:
1) Retract the sleeve at the receiver end of the hold-open rod and compress it to
disengage the rod from the receiver.
2) Engage the hold-open rod end on the receiver on the fan cowl panel with the curved
lock end facing away from the fan cowl.
(e) Do the steps again to engage the aft hold-open rod on the fan cowl panel.

fan cowl panel. The manual procedure uses four persons to remove the fan cowl panel. The

WARNING

OR GUSTY WIND CONDITIONS. DO NOT TRY TO REMOVE THE FAN COWL

(b) The maximum wind velocity is not more than 40 knots.

E. Fan Cowl Panel Removal (Manual Procedure)
SUBTASK 71-11-02-020-002-F00
(1) Release the three latches along the mating line of the fan cowl panels:
(a) Push the trigger to release the safety catch and pull the handle to release the latch.
1) Use a screwdriver in the slot if more leverage is necessary.

71-11-02
SUBTASK 71-11-02-020-003-F00
CAUTION
MAKE SURE YOU USE A MINIMUM OF FOUR PERSONS TO REMOVE THE
FAN COWL PANEL. USE THREE PERSONS TO HOLD THE PANEL AND ONE
TO DISENGAGE THE FAN COWL CLEVIS FROM THE STRUT LUGS. THE
LEFT FAN COWL PANEL WEIGHS APPROXIMATELY 80 POUNDS (36 KG),
AND THE RIGHT FAN COWL PANEL WEIGHS APPROXIMATELY 96 POUNDS
(44 KG). IF YOU DO NOT USE THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF PERSONS,
DAMAGE TO THE FAN COWL PANEL, STRUT , INLET AND THRUST
REVERSER CAN OCCUR.
(2) Do these steps to remove the fan cowl panel [1]:
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU OPEN THE FAN COWL PANELS. OPEN THE
FAN COWL PANEL JUST UNTIL ONE PERSON CAN GO UNDER THE
FAN COWL AND DISENGAGE THE PINS. IF YOU OPEN THEM TOO
MUCH, DAMAGE TO THE STRUT CAN OCCUR.
(a) Use three persons to hold the fan cowl panel [1] open.
(b) Use the fourth person to disengage each quick-release pin as follows:
NOTE: There is a quick-release pin for each of the three attach points. Each
quick-release pin is permanently attached to the strut.
1) Remove the safety pin from the end of the quick-release pin.
2) Release the quick release pin with the button on the end.
3) Do the above steps again for the other two quick release pins.
(c) Move the fan cowl panel [1] away from the engine.
(d) Put the fan cowl panel [1] on a pallet or other suitable surface.
NOTE: Put the fan cowl panel with its top and bottom edges on the pallet or surface.

WARNING

(3) Do these steps to remove the fan cowl panel [1]:

71-11-02
(b) Disengage the quick-release pin at an outer hinge as follows:
NOTE: There is a quick-release pin for each of the three attach points. Each
quick-release pin is permanently attached to the strut.
1) Remove the safety pin from the end of the quick-release pin.
2) Release the quick-release pin with the button on the end and remove the pin.
3) Install the drift pin from the sling kit at the outer hinge.
4) Do the above steps again at the remaining outer hinge.
(c) Disengage and remove the quick-release pin at the center hinge.
(d) Adjust the position of the fan cowl panel [1], until the drift pins can be easily removed.
(e) Remove the drift pin at each outer hinge.
(f) Carefully move the fan cowl panel [1] away from the engine.
(g) Put the fan cowl panel [1] on a pallet or other suitable surface.
1) Put the fan cowl panel [1] with its top and bottom edges on the pallet or surface.
(h) If it is necessary, remove the fan cowl sling, SPL-2108, from the fan cowl panel [1].

E. Fan Cowl Panel Installation (Manual Procedure)
SUBTASK 71-11-02-420-002-F00
WARNING
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU MOVE THE FAN COWL PANEL. BECAUSE THE
LEFT FAN COWL PANEL WEIGHS 80 POUNDS (36 KG) AND THE RIGHT FAN
COWL PANEL WEIGHS 96 POUNDS (44 KG), INJURIES TO PERSONS AND
DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU PUT THE FAN COWL PANEL ON THE HINGES.
DAMAGE TO THE HINGES, STRUT AND FAN COWL PANEL CAN OCCUR.
CAUTION
MAKE SURE YOU USE A MINIMUM OF FOUR PERSONS TO INSTALL THE
FAN COWL PANEL. IF YOU DO NOT USE THE MINIMUM NUMBER OF
PERSONS, DAMAGE TO THE FAN COWL PANEL, STRUT , INLET AND
THRUST REVERSER CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to install the fan cowl panel [1]:
(a) Use three persons to lift the fan cowl panel [1] to the engine and align the fan cowl
clevises with the strut lugs.
(b) Use the fourth person to install the quick-release pins.
(c) At two of the three locations, install the quick-release pins to attach the strut lugs to the
fan cowl clevises.
NOTE: For the forward and aft attach points, the quick-release pins are installed from the
aft side. For the center attach point, the quick-release pin is installed from the
forward side.
NOTE: The quick-release pins and the safety pins are permanently attached to the strut.
1) Install the safety pin through the hole in the end of each quick-release pin.
(d) At the remaining location, install the quick-release pin.
NOTE: You can apply a maximum force of 30 pounds (133 Newtons) to the fan cowl at
the hinge locations to align the hinges.
1) Install the safety pin through the hole in the end of the quick-release pin.
(e) Slowly close, but do not latch, the fan cowl panel [1].
SUBTASK 71-11-02-420-003-F00
(2) If you replaced the fan cowl panel, do this task: Fan Cowl Panel Latch Adjustment,

SUBTASK 71-11-02-010-004-F00
CAUTION

DAMAGE TO THE LATCH.
(3) Close the three latches along the mating line of the fan cowl panels:

2. Fan Cowl Panel Latch Adjustment
(Figure 501)
A. General
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to adjust the fan cowl panel latch.
(2) Latch adjustments are necessary to get the correct clearance at the mating line of the fan cowl
panels and to get the correct latch tension.
(a) The clearance adjustment uses laminated washers at each latch position.
(b) The latch tension adjustment gives the correct force to close the latch handle.
(3) Do the latch adjustments in the sequence given.
(4) Do the latch adjustments after the removal or the replacement of these components:
(a) The fan cowl panels
(b) The latches or the latch keepers on the fan cowl panels
(c) The inlet cowl, the thrust reverser or the engine.
(5) The latch adjustments for the fan cowl panels are written with the inlet cowl installed and the
thrust reverser closed, latched and correctly adjusted.

end of the latch handle and close the latch with a force of 15-25 pounds (67-111 N).

(Views A-A and B-B):
1) Keep the latch handle open in the free travel position of approximately 15 degrees.
2) Put a 5/32 inch (4 mm) hexagonal wrench into the slots of the latch keeper.
3) Turn the wrench in the aft direction to increase the latch tension or the forward
direction to decrease the tension.
(f) Measure the clearance at the mating line between the fan cowl panels at each latch.
1) Make sure that the clearance is 0.120 ± 0.090 inch (3.048 ± 2.286 mm) (VIEW A).
(g) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00.
(h) Measure the clay at the striker plate and the alignment pin flange at each latch.
1) There must be no measureable clearance between the striker plate and the latch
housing or the alignment pin flange and the latch housing.
(i) If there is no clearance, remove the clay from the latch with a clean cotton cloth.
1) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.
2) Do this procedure: Latch T ension Adjustment.
(j) If there is a clearance, continue to the subsequent step.
SUBTASK 71-11-03-820-002-F00
(2) Do these steps to remove the laminated washers [7] from the striker plate [6] at each latch
(View D-D):
(a) Remove the nut [9], the washer [8] and the bolt [5] that attach the striker plate [6] to the
latch keeper housing.
(b) Remove the striker plate [6] and the laminated washers [7] and keep the laminated
washers for the subsequent installation.
(c) Install the striker plate [6], the bolt [5], the washer [8] and the nut [9].
1) Tighten the nut [9] to 18-25 pound-inches (2.03-2.82 Newton-meters).
SUBTASK 71-11-03-820-003-F00
(3) Do these steps to remove the laminated washers [1] from the alignment pin [2] at each latch
(View A):
(a) Remove the nut [4] and the washer [3] that attach the alignment pin [2] to the keeper
housing.
(b) Remove the alignment pin [2], and the laminated washers [1] and keep the laminated
washers for the subsequent installation.
(c) Install the alignment pin [2], the washer [3], and the nut [4].
71-11-03
1) Tighten the nut [4] to 270-350 pound-inches (30.50-39.54 Newton-meters).
SUBTASK 71-11-03-820-004-F00
(4) Do these steps to find the correct thickness of the washer [1] and the washer [7] to install at
each latch.
(a) Apply clay, G02020 to the striker plate and the alignment pin flange.
(b) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.
1) Engage the forward and aft latch hooks in the latch keepers.
(c) Adjust the forward and aft latch keepers to get these conditions:
1) A force of 15-25 pounds (67-111 N) to close the latch
2) A clearance of 0.120 ± 0.090 inch (3.048 ± 2.286 mm) at the mating line between
the fan cowl panels.
NOTE: A tapered clearance between the fan cowl panels from the forward end to
the aft end is permitted.
3) Do these steps for the adjustment:
a) Keep the latch handle open in the free travel position of approximately 15
degrees.
b) Put a 5/32 inch (4 mm) hexagonal wrench into the slots of the keeper.
c) Turn the wrench in the aft direction to increase the latch tension or the forward
direction to decrease the tension.
(d) Do this task: Open the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00.
(e) Measure the thickness of the clay at the striker plate and alignment pin flange at each
latch.
1) This is the correct thickness of laminated washer [1] and the washer [7] to install.
SUBTASK 71-11-03-820-005-F00
(5) Do these steps to install the correct thickness of laminated washer [1] and the washer [7] at the
striker plate [6] and the alignment pin [2] at each latch (View D-D):
(a) Remove the clay from the striker plate, alignment pin flange, and latch keeper housing
with a clean cotton cloth.
(b) Remove the nut [9], the washer [8], the bolt [5], and the striker plate [6].
(c) Adjust the quantity of the laminated washer [1] and the washer [7] to agree with the
correct thickness that you found.
(d) Install the striker plate [6], laminated washers [7], and bolt [5] with the laminated washers
between the striker plate and the keeper housing.
(e) Install the washer [8] and the nut [9].
NOTE: Put laminated washers or equivalent washers between the keeper housing and
the nut to keep the correct fastener grip length.
1) Tighten the nut [9] to 18-25 pound-inches (2.03-2.82 Newton-meters).
(f) Remove the nut [4], the washer [3], and the alignment pin [2].
(g) Install the necessary laminated washers [1] and the alignment pin [2] with the laminated
washers between the pin flange and the keeper housing.
(h) Install the washer [3] and the nut [4].
NOTE: Put laminated washers or equivalent washers between the keeper housing and
the nut to keep the correct fastener grip length.
71-11-03
1) Tighten the nut [4] to 270-350 pound-inches (30.50-39.54 Newton-meters).
SUBTASK 71-11-03-410-001-F00
(6) Do these steps for a clearance check of the washer installation:
(a) Do this task: Close the Fan Cowl Panels, TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00.
1) Engage the latch hooks in the keepers in this sequence:
a) Engage the center latch hook.
b) Engage the forward latch hook.
c) Engage the aft latch hook.
(b) Make sure that the striker plate and the alignment pin flange touch fully with the latch
housings at each latch.
1) If there is a clearance at one or more positions, do these steps again:
a) Remove the laminated washers.
b) Find the correct thickness of washers with clay.
c) Install the laminated washers.
d) Do the clearance check of the washer installation.
2) If there are no clearances, do this procedure: Latch T ension Adjustment.
G. Fan Cowl Panel Latch Tension Adjustment
SUBTASK 71-11-03-820-006-F00
CAUTION
DO NOT USE MORE THAN 60 POUNDS (267 N) OF FORCE TO PUSH THE
LATCH HANDLE CLOSED. TOO MUCH FORCE CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
THE EQUIPMENT .
(1) Do these steps to adjust the latch tension:
(a) Disengage one of the three latches.
(b) Put a push/pull gauge (0-150 lbs), STD-1099 approximately 1.0 inch (25.4 mm) from the
end of the latch handle and close the latch with a force of 40-60 pounds (178-267 N).
1) If it is necessary, adjust the latch keeper to get the correct force on the latch handle.
a) Keep the latch handle open in the free travel position of approximately 15
degrees.
b) Put a 5/32 inch (4 mm) hexagonal wrench into the slots of the keeper.
c) Turn the wrench in the aft direction to increase the latch tension or the forward
direction to decrease the tension.
2) Adjust the latch tension for the remaining latches.
NOTE: Make sure the trigger lock of the latch handle engages to hold the handle in
the closed position.

G. T12 Access/Pressure Relief Door Latch Release Test
SUBTASK 71-11-06-970-001-F00
(1) Calculate the minimum and the maximum torque for the length of the wrench that you use with
the formula (Table 501).
71-11-06
Table 501/71-11-06-993-805-F00
LATCH RELEASE TEST - TORQUE CALCULATION
TORQUE pound-inch = 0.53(P)(L)/(L + 1.5 inch)
Where P = Latch open load in pounds
L = Wrench effective length in inches Figure 502
For METRIC, N.m = 0.13442(P)(L)/(L + 38.1 mm)
P in Newtons, L in mm
Pmin-Pmax must be 50-65 pounds (222.4-289.1 Newtons)
EXAMPLE CALCULATION (use Pmin-Pmax, L =12 inch)
TORQUE minimum = 0.53(50)(12)/(12+1.5) = 23.6 pound-inches
TORQUE maximum (use Pmax = 65) = 30.6 pound-inches
For METRIC, let L =304.8 mm
TORQUE min = 0.13442(222.4)(304.8)/(304.8+38.1) = 2.66 N.m
TORQUE maximum (use Pmax = 289.1) = 3.46 N.m
(a) The correct load (Pmin-Pmax) to open the latch is 50 lbf (222.4 N) - 65 lbf (289.1 N).
(b) Find the effective length of the torque wrench (View A-A, Figure 502).
(c) For a 12 in. (304.8 mm) wrench, the correct torque is 23.6 in-lb (2.67 N·m) - 30.6 in-lb
(3.46 N·m).
SUBTASK 71-11-06-820-007-F00
(2) Do these steps to do the latch test:
(a) Put the torque adapter on the torque wrench.
1) The torque adapter is part of the adapter equipment, SPL-4409.

G. Chip Detector Access/Pressure Relief Door Latch Release Test
SUBTASK 71-11-07-970-001-F00
(1) Calculate the minimum and maximum torque for the length of the wrench that you use with the
formula (Table 501).
71-11-07
Table 501/71-11-07-993-805-F00
LATCH RELEASE TEST - TORQUE CALCULATION
TORQUE pound-inch = 0.53(P)(L)/(L + 1.5 inch)
Where P = Latch open load in pounds
L = Wrench effective length in inches Figure 502
For METRIC, N.m = 0.13442(P)(L)/(L + 38.1 mm)
P in Newtons, L in mm
Pmin-Pmax must be 63-77 pounds (280.2-342.5 Newtons)
EXAMPLE CALCULATION (use Pmin-Pmax, L =12 inch)
TORQUE minimum = 0.53(63)(12)/(12+1.5) = 29.7 pound-inches
TORQUE maximum (use Pmax = 77) = 36.3 pound-inches
For METRIC, let L =304.8 mm
TORQUE min = 0.13442(280.2)(304.8)/(304.8+38.1) = 3.35 N.m
TORQUE maximum (use Pmax = 342.5) = 4.10 N.m
(a) The correct load (Pmin-Pmax) to open the door is 63 lbf (280.2 N) - 77 lbf (342.5 N).
(b) Find the effective length of the torque wrench (View A-A, Figure 502).
(c) For a 12 in. (304.8 mm) wrench, the correct torque is 29.7 in-lb (3.36 N·m) - 36.3 in-lb
(4.10 N·m).
SUBTASK 71-11-07-820-007-F00
(2) Do these steps to do the load test:

(b) Put the torque adapter on the torque wrench.
1) The torque adapter is part of the adapter equipment, SPL-4409.
(c) Put the thinner end of the adapter tightly into the slot on the latch.
(d) Apply a right-angle force on the torque wrench in the aft direction until the latch opens.

WARNING

(d) Apply a thin coat of PR-1200 primer, C00580, to the faying surfaces of the vortex control
device [1] and seal [2].
1) Use clean gloves when handling primed surfaces.

percent or higher.
1) If the relative humidity is less than 50 percent, dry the primer for 3 hours at room
temperature.
SUBTASK 71-11-09-390-001-F01
(2) Apply adhesive Dow Corning 90-006 sealant, A00066 (or alternate RTV88 sealant, A01079).
WARNING
DO NOT GET THE ADHESIVE IN YOUR EYES OR ON YOUR SKIN.
WEAR SAFETY GLASSES TO PROTECT YOUR EYES. WEAR
POLYETHYLENE GLOVES TO PROTECT YOUR HANDS. INJURIES TO
PERSONNEL COULD OCCUR.
(a) Mix the two parts in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.

A01079) 10-12 MIL thick, to the faying surfaces of the vortex control device [1] and
rubber seal [2].
1) Apply the adhesive within 4 hours after primer application.
2) Install seal [2] onto the vortex control device [1] within 5-10 minutes after adhesive
has been applied.
(c) Place seal [2] onto the vortex control device [1].
1) Make sure that seal [2] is correctly aligned on the vortex control device [1].

(e) Clamp seal [2] to the vortex control device [1].
1) Use only enough pressure to keep seal [2] in place.
(f) Cure the adhesive for 24 hours at room temperature.

200°F (93.33°C) for 2 hours.
