E. VCD Seal Repair
SUBTASK 71-11-09-210-001-F00
(1) Examine the outer surface of the VCD seal [1] for erosion damage.
(a) A VCD seal [1] with erosion damage can continue in service with these conditions:
1) No portion of the seal may be missing from underneath the VCD where the seal
interfaces with the inlet cowl outer barrel surface.
2) No gaps allowed under seal where it interfaces with the inlet cowl outer barrel
surface.
3) No tears are allowed if the tear extends aft underneath the VCD.
(b) If you find one or more of the above conditions, do one of these steps:
1) Replace the VCD seal [1] (TASK 71-11-09-000-801-F01 and
TASK 71-11-09-420-801-F01).
2) Do the temporary repair.
3) If the seal damage does not extend under the VCD, and has no gaps and there is
no portion of the seal missing, do the trim repair.
SUBTASK 71-11-09-350-001-F00
(2) Do these steps to repair (trim) the VCD seal [1]:
71-11-09
(a) Make a trim template for the VCD seal [1] as follows:
1) Determine how far aft the leading edge of the VCD seal [1] can be trimmed without
creating a gap between the underside of the seal and the external surface of the
outer barrel skin.
2) Make a mark (horse shoe shaped) on the eroded part/area of the seal to be
removed.
3) Make a trim template with 6 in. (152 mm) by 6 in. (152 mm) by 0.050 in. (1.27 mm)
thick, A286 CRES to align with the shape of the seal material to be removed.
4) Make the template with 0.50 in. (12.70 mm) radius corners.
a) Contour the template to align the external surface of the outer barrel with light
finger pressure.
5) De-burr and remove all sharp edges from the template.
6) Apply teflon tape around the edges of the template to prevent damage to the outer
barrel external surface during installation.
(b) Install the template as follows:
1) Open the fan cowl panel and safety it in the open position to get access to the inlet
cowl (TASK 71-11-02-010-801-F00).
2) Carefully put the template on the outer barrel external surface where the VCD
seal [1] will touch when the fan cowl panel is closed.
3) Make a mark around the edges of the installed position for the template.
CAUTION
BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU APPLY THE TEFLON TAPE OR INSTALL
THE TRIM PLATE. DAMAGE TO THE TOP OF THE PAINT COAT CAN
OCCUR.
4) Apply teflon tape or equivalent to the entire area where you will install the template
as follows:
a) Apply the tape approximately 2.0 in. (50.8 mm) beyond the edge of the
template on all sides for added protection.
5) Attach the trim plate in position with teflon tape or equivalent.
6) Close the fan cowl panel and make sure that the VCD seal [1] is centered on the
template (TASK 71-11-02-410-801-F00).
(c) Trim the VCD seal [1]:
1) Carefully place the template over the horse shoe shaped mark on the top of the
VCD seal [1] and trim the eroded part of the seal with a sharp knife.
a) Make sure that there is sufficient seal material below the VCD after the repair.
NOTE: The seal material prevents damage to the inlet cowl and VCD during
flight conditions.
2) Make sure that there are no tears or frayed edges after the repair that no gap is
apparent.
3) Carefully remove the seal trimmings and the template.
4) Open the fan cowl panel and carefully remove the teflon tape and all traces of glue
or /adhesive on the external surface of the Outer Barrel skin.
71-11-09
WARNING
DO NOT GET ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IN YOUR MOUTH, EYES, OR
ON YOUR SKIN. DO NOT BREATHE THE FUMES FROM THE
ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL. KEEP THE ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL AWAY
FROM SPARKS, FLAME, AND HEAT . ISOPROPYL ALCOHOL IS
POISONOUS AND FLAMMABLE, WHICH CAN CAUSE INJURIES TO
PERSONS AND DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT .
5) Clean the area with a lint-free cloth, G01043, made moist with alcohol, B00130.
a) Remove all unwanted material and wipe dry with lint-free cloth, G01043.
(d) Examine the VCD seal [1].
1) Close the fan cowl panel.
2) Visually examine the VCD seal [1] to outer barrel external skin interface.
3) Make sure that there is no gap under seal where it interfaces with the inlet cowl
outer barrel.
4) If a gap is found, replace the VCD seal [1].
5) If you do not find a gap, continue the airplane in service.
SUBTASK 71-11-09-350-002-F00
(3) Do these steps to temporary repair the VCD seal [1] to continue service for up to 40 days:
NOTE: This is permitted as long as no report of other damage.
NOTE: This repair is applicable to damage on the VCD seal. The entire seal may be recessed
under the VCD footprint 0.150 in. (3.810 mm).
(a) Clean the inlet cowl outer barrel outer surface near the VCD leading edge at the
damaged area of the VCD seal [1] with isopropyl alcohol, B00676 [CP1041], and a clean
lint-free cloth, G01043.
NOTE: Wipe the surface dry before the solvent evaporates.
(b) Visually inspect the outer surface of the inlet cowl outer barrel outer surface and the
leading edge of the VCD for damage.
NOTE: If you find additional damage, contact Boeing.
(c) Remove all loose VCD parts or protruding seal parts.
NOTE: All amounts of seal material can be removed or missing as long as there is no
seal gap between the VCD and the inlet cowl.
(d) Apply aluminum speed tape, G51102 [CP2515], to cover the gap for the temporary repair
as follows:
NOTE: This is the gap between the VCD and the outer surface of the inlet cowl.
1) Make sure that the tape extends 3 in. (76.2 mm) past the footprint of the missing
portion of the seal.
2) Make sure that you apply each ply of aluminum speed tape, G51102 [CP2515], with
a 50% bias overlap.
NOTE: There should be no gap between the strips.
(e) If you will open the fan cowl after the speed tape application, make sure that you do the
procedure again to maintain the aerodynamic seal.
(f) Do a daily visual inspection of the temporary repair area to make sure that the damage
did not grow.
1) If it is necessary, re-apply aluminum speed tape, G51102 [CP2515].
71-11-09
(g) Replace the VCD seal [1] before the expiration of the 40 day extension.

(1) Examine the forward engine mount for these signs of damage.

1) Cracks to the bearing (race) are not permitted.

2. Forward Engine Mount Removal
(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) This task provides the instructions on how to remove the forward engine mount.
(2) The forward engine mount is found at the 12:00 o'clock position on the outer case of the fan
frame.
(3) You must remove the engine from the strut before you can remove the forward engine mount.
B. References
Reference Title
71-00-02-000-801-F00 Power Plant - Removal (P/B 401)
C. Location Zones
Zone Area
411 Engine 1 - Engine
421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Prepare for the Removal
SUBTASK 71-21-01-010-001-F00
(1) Do this task: Power Plant - Removal, TASK 71-00-02-000-801-F00.
E. Forward Engine Mount Removal
SUBTASK 71-21-01-020-001-F00
(1) Do these steps to remove the hangar fitting assembly [1]:
(a) Remove the three nuts [4] and the end caps [3] from the pawl pins [2] in the hangar fitting
assembly [1].
1) PAWL PINS WITH A SPRING LOADED PAWL; Hold the spring-loaded pawl in while
you remove the nuts [4].
NOTE: You can use a metal or hard plastic tube or another nut to hold the pawl in.
2) PAWL PINS WITH A COTTER PIN; Remove the cotter pin before you remove the
nuts [4].
(b) Remove the three pawl pins [2] and the two washers [11].
(c) Remove the hangar fitting assembly [1].
SUBTASK 71-21-01-020-002-F00
(2) Do these steps to remove the fan case fitting [5]:
(a) Remove the four bolts [6] and the washers [7] at the center of the fitting.
(b) Remove the six bolts [6] and the bolts [8], the six washers [7], and the two bushings [9] at
the outer positions.
71-21-01
(c) Remove the fan case fitting [5].

F . Forward Engine Mount Installation
SUBTASK 71-21-01-640-001-F00
(1) Apply the Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006 to the bolt threads and under the bolts [6]
heads and the bolts [8] heads.
SUBTASK 71-21-01-020-003-F00
(2) Install the fan case fitting [5] as follows:
(a) Put the fan case fitting [5] on the fan case and align the holes.
(b) Install the two longer bolts [8], the washers [7] and the bushings [9] at the outer positions.
NOTE: Make sure the washers [7] are installed under the bolt [8] with the countersunk
side up.
(c) Install the four bolts [6] and the washers [7] at the outer positions.
71-21-01
(d) Install the four bolts [6] and the washers [7] at the center of the fitting.
(e) Tighten the ten bolts [6] and the bolts [8] for the fan case fitting to 585 in-lb (66 N·m) to
715 in-lb (81 N·m).
NOTE: Make sure that the bolts [6] and the bolts [8] are tightened equally.
(f) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912 or safety cable kit, G50375 to the four
bolts [6] at the center of the fitting.
NOTE: The safety cable kit, G50375 may be used as an alternate to the MS20995NC32
lockwire, G01912.
1) Attach a lockwire to the two forward bolts.
2) Attach a lockwire to the two aft bolts.
(g) Install the MS20995NC32 lockwire, G01912 or safety cable kit, G50375 on the three
bolts [6] and the bolts [8] at the outer positions.
NOTE: The safety cable kit, G50375 may be used as an alternate to the MS20995NC32
lockwire, G01912.
1) Install Tyco Fluoroelastomer Tubing, G50043 or Viton sleeve, G50044 on the
lockwire where it rubs against the fan case fitting.
SUBTASK 71-21-01-020-004-F00
(3) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006 to the pawl pin threads and shanks; and, to the
bushings, bearings, and bores.
SUBTASK 71-21-01-020-005-F00
(4) Do these steps to install the hangar fitting assembly [1]:
(a) Put the hangar fitting assembly [1] on the fan case fitting [5] and align the holes for the
pawl pins.
1) Make sure to install the hangar fitting assembly [1] with the shear pins on the
forward edge.
(b) Install the three pawl pins [2] with the head on the forward side of the mount.
NOTE: The fit for the middle pawl is looser. There is more clearance between the pawl
pin and the bushing in the fan case fitting.
(c) Install the washer [11] at each outer pin location.
NOTE: The washer [11] can be installed on the forward or aft side of the bearing.
1) Make sure that the chamfer side of the washer [11] is against the bearing.
(d) Install the three end caps [3] and nuts [4].
1) Make sure that the flat side of the end cap [3] is against the pin shoulder.
2) Tighten the three nuts to 290 in-lb (33 N·m) to 510 in-lb (58 N·m).
a) You can apply the torque to the nut or the head of the pin.
3) PAWL PINS WITH A SPRING LOADED PAWL; Make sure the spring-loaded pawl
on the pins are in the extended position after the nuts are tight.
4) PAWL PINS WITH A COTTER PIN; Install the cotter pin.
G. Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition
SUBTASK 71-21-01-410-001-F00
(1) Do this task: Power Plant - Installation, TASK 71-00-02-400-801-F00.

(Figure 401)
A. General
(1) This task contains the instructions to remove the thrust link assembly.
(2) The thrust links are installed between the fan frame and the aft engine mount.
(3) You can only remove and install one thrust link at a time with the power plant installed on the
strut because of the load.

F . Thrust Link Assembly Removal
SUBTASK 71-21-02-020-001-F00
CAUTION
DO NOT REMOVE THE TWO THRUST LINKS AT THE SAME TIME. IF YOU DO
NOT OBEY THE INSTRUCTIONS, THE ENGINE CAN MOVE REARWARD AND
DAMAGE TO THE ENGINE FAIRINGS CAN OCCUR.
(1) Do these steps to remove the left or right thrust link assembly [1]:
(a) For the left thrust link assembly [1], remove the Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) cooling air
tube (TASK 72-32-00-200-804-F00).
(b) For the right thrust link assembly [1], do these steps, if it is necessary:
1) Disconnect the T3 sensor from the T3 sensor bracket.
2) Disconnect the T3 sensor bracket from the engine.
(c) Remove the nut [3] and end cap [2] at each end of the thrust link assembly [1].
1) PAWL PINS WITH A SPRING LOADED PAWL; Hold the spring-loaded pawl in while
you remove the nut [3].
NOTE: You can use the thread protector, a metal or hard plastic tube, or another
nut to hold the pawl in.
2) PAWL PINS WITH A COTTER PIN; Remove the cotter pin before you remove the
nut [3].
(d) Install a thread protectors from the equipment, SPL-2438, on the pawl pins [5] at each
end of the thrust link assembly [1].
(e) Remove the pawl pin [5] and washer [4] from the aft end of the thrust link assembly [1].
(f) Remove the pawl pin [5] and washer [4] from the forward end of the thrust link
assembly [1].

G. Thrust Link Assembly Installation
SUBTASK 71-21-02-640-001-F00
(1) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the threads and shank of the pawl pins [5]
(View A-A and View B-B, Figure 401).
SUBTASK 71-21-02-480-001-F00
(2) Install the thread protector from the equipment, SPL-2438, on the pawl pin [5] for the forward
end of the thrust link assembly [1].
SUBTASK 71-21-02-420-001-F00
(3) Do these steps to install the left or right thrust link assembly [1]:
71-21-02
(a) Apply Pure Nickel Special compound, D00006, to the spherical bearing bores and ball flat
surfaces of the thrust link fitting on the engine fan frame and aft engine mount attaching
points.
(b) Put the thrust link assembly [1] on the engine.
1) Align the aft end of the thrust link assembly [1] with the aft engine mount and align
the forward end of the thrust link assembly [1] with the thrust link fitting.
(c) Install the pawl pin [5] and washer [4] at the aft end of the thrust link assembly [1].
1) Apply RTV 159 sealant, A00933, or RTV 106 adhesive, A00081, between the
washer [4] and underneath the bolt head of the pawl pin [5].
2) Put the countersunk side of the washer [4] against the head of the pawl pin [5].
(d) Remove the thread protector from the pawl pin [5] at the aft end of the thrust link
assembly [1].
(e) Install the end cap [2] and nut [3] at the aft end of the thrust link assembly [1].
1) Make sure that the flat side of the end cap [2] is against the shoulder of the pawl
pin [5].
2) PAWL PINS WITH A SPRING LOADED PAWL; Make sure that the spring-loaded
pawl is in the extended position after you install the nut [3].
(f) Install the pawl pin [5], washer [4], and washer [6] at the forward end of the thrust link
assembly [1].
1) Apply RTV 159 sealant, A00933, or RTV 106 adhesive, A00081, between the
washer [4] and underneath the bolt head of the pawl pin [5].
2) Put the countersunk side of the washer [4] against the head of the pawl pin [5].
3) Put the countersunk side of the washer [6] against the spherical bearing.
RYR 006, 007, 013 PRE SL 737-71-049
4) The washer [6] is the recommended installation.
RYR ALL
(g) Remove the thread protector from the pawl pin [5] at the forward end of the thrust link
assembly [1].
(h) Install the end cap [2] and nut [3] at the forward end of the thrust link assembly [1].
1) Make sure that the flat side of the end cap [2] is against the shoulder of the pawl
pins [5].
2) PAWL PINS WITH A SPRING LOADED PAWL; Make sure that the spring-loaded
pawl is in the extended position after you install the nut [3].
(i) Torque the nuts [3] or the heads of the pawl pins [5] to 290 in-lb (32.8 N·m) - 510 in-lb
(57.6 N·m) at each end of the thrust link assembly [1].
NOTE: You can apply the torque to the nut or to the head of the pawl pin.
(j) PAWL PINS WITH A COTTER PIN; Install the cotter pin.
(k) For the left thrust link assembly [1], install the Low Pressure Turbine (LPT) cooling air
tube (TASK 72-32-00-200-804-F00).
(l) For the right thrust link assembly [1], re-connect the T3 sensor bracket to the engine and
the T3 sensor to the T3 sensor bracket, if disconnected.

421 Engine 2 - Engine
D. Thrust Links Visual Inspection
SUBTASK 71-21-02-210-003-F00
(1) Examine the thrust links for damage:
(a) Cracks are not permitted.
(b) Nicks are not permitted.
(c) Dents are not permitted.
(d) Scratches are not permitted.
(e) Pitting is not permitted.
(f) Fretting is not permitted.
NOTE: Fretting is caused when two adjacent pieces of metal rub one another.
(g) Pickup is not permitted.
NOTE: Pickup occurs when material is moved from one surface to a surface which it
touches.
(h) High metal is not permitted.
NOTE: High metal is metal which is pushed above the surface adjacent to scratches or
other damage.
(i) Bushing movement is not permitted.
SUBTASK 71-21-02-210-004-F00
(2) If damage is found on the thrust links, refer to the Structural Repair Manual for the allowable
damage limits (SRM 54-70-90).
(a) Replace the thrust links component, if it is more than the allowable damage limits.
71-21-02
1) Do this task: Thrust Link Assembly Removal, TASK 71-21-02-000-801-F00.
2) Do this task: Thrust Link Assembly Installation, TASK 71-21-02-400-801-F00.
SUBTASK 71-21-02-210-005-F00
(3) Examine the thrust link for worn areas.
NOTE: The thrust links can be damaged from contact with the thrust reverser insulation
blanket .
(a) If you find signs of wear on the thrust links.
1) Do this task: Thrust Links Detailed Inspection, TASK 71-21-02-210-803-F00.

SUBTASK 71-21-03-020-001-F00
(1) Disconnect the two thrust links [2] from the aft engine mount [1].
(a) Remove the nut [11], end cap [12], washer [13] and pawl pin [14] at each thrust link [2].
1) PAWL PINS WITH A SPRING LOADED PAWL;
Hold the spring-loaded pawl in while you remove the nut [11].

Remove the cotter pin before you remove the nut [11].

D30212 (D30412), DP0112

3) Ignition Box 1, DP0102
4) The A/C receptacle on the N1 Speed Sensor, DP0103.

D30256 (D30456), DP0256

3) Ignition Box 2, DP0201.
SUBTASK 71-51-03-420-003-F00
(3) To install the MW0303 harness [21], do these steps (Figure 403):
(a) Put the MW0303 harness [21] on the engine.
(b) Connect the harness to these components:
71-51-03
1) The service disconnect panel on the right side of the fan cowl support beam
D30224 (D30424), DP0324

(b) Connect the harness to these components:
1) The service disconnect panel on the right side of the fan cowl support beam
D30260 (D30460), DP0460
2) The J4 receptacle on the aft side of the EEC, DP0404.
SUBTASK 71-51-03-420-005-F00
(5) To install the MW0312 harness [41], do these steps (Figure 405):
(a) Put the MW0312 harness [41] on the engine.
CAUTION
DO NOT TIGHTEN THE PLUG COUPLING RINGS TOO MUCH. DO NOT
USE WATER PUMP PLIERS, PIPE WRENCHES, OR VICE GRIPS TO
TIGHTEN THE COUPLING RING OR DAMAGE TO THE ELECTRICAL
CONNECTOR CAN OCCUR.
(b) Connect the harness to these components:
1) The service disconnect panel on the left side of the fan cowl support beam D30234
(D30434), DP1234
2) The Start Valve, DP1202
3) The N2 Speed Sensor, DP1201
4) The IDG, DP1205 and DP1206
5) The EDP , DP1204
6) The HMU, DP1203 and DP1207.

(6) To install the MW0313 harness [51], do these steps (Figure 406):

1) The service disconnect panel on the right side of the fan cowl support beam
D30228 (D30428), DP1328
2) The inlet cowl TAI valve, DP1302 and DP1303
3) The oil quantity transmitter, DP1301
4) The Number 1 Bearing Vibration Sensor, found aft of the oil tank and above the
engine nameplate, DP1304.
SUBTASK 71-51-03-020-009-F00
(7) Make sure that the connectors are fully engaged and do not move.

torn.

71-71-00-200-801-F00Engine Vents and Drains InspectionPDF p. 803
Open original AMM PDF - page 803 ↗ 
2. Engine Vents and Drains Inspection
(Figure 601, Figure 602, Figure 603, and Figure 604)
A. General
(1) This task estimates the condition of the Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) by the rate of fluid
leakage at the drains.
(2) Leaks from the drain can occur on an engine that does not operate or during an engine start.
These leaks are not unusual, and may stop after the engine operates at minimum idle for five
(5) minutes.
(3) This task examines the engine and strut drains in these areas:
(a) Below the engine fan case for Accessory Gear Box (AGB)-mounted and engine core
component drains, the forward sump and the service disconnect (strut) drain.
(b) Inside the primary plug assembly for the aft sump drain.

F . Engine Vents and Drains Inspection
SUBTASK 71-71-00-790-001-F00
(1) Do a visual check of the drains for signs of leakage (Figure 601, Figure 602).
NOTE: Leaks from the drain can occur on an engine that does not operate or during an
engine start. These leaks are not unusual, and may stop after the engine operates at
idle power for 5 minutes.
SUBTASK 71-71-00-790-002-F00
(2) If there are no signs of leakage, the engine is serviceable.
(a) Continue to the task in the paragraph, Put the Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition.
SUBTASK 71-71-00-790-011-F00
(3) These leakage limits are given in threshold limits and serviceable limits:
NOTE: The limits apply for static leaks (engine off) and dynamic leaks (engine on).
(a) For fuel leaks:
1) If the total leakage rate from the drains is less than the threshold limit, you can
continue to operate the engine (maintenance action is not necessary).
2) If the total leakage rate from the drains is more than the threshold limit, but less
than the serviceable limit, corrective action must be done before 25 flight cycles.
3) If the total leakage rate from the drains is more than the serviceable limit, you must
do the corrective action.
(b) For oil leaks:
1) If the leakage rate is more than the threshold limit, but less than the serviceable
limit, you can continue to operate the engine until maintenance can be done.
2) If the leakage rate is more than the serviceable limit, maintenance must be done
before you operate the engine again.
(c) For hydraulic leaks:
1) If the total leakage rate from the strut drain is more than the serviceable limit, you
must do the corrective action.
(d) Use the applicable limit in the paragraph, Leakage Limits and Corrective Action.
(e) If maintenance action is not necessary, continue to the task in the paragraph, Put the
Airplane Back to Its Usual Condition.
